call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Edit ONLY the typography organization of the supplied source poster. Return one finished flat portrait poster, 2:3.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

The existing centered white horizontal title crosses the giant dark stems like a separate digital overlay. Replace that title with an integrated, matte painted-letter composition on the existing illuminated wall wedge between the small real plant and its much larger cast presence. Remove the original title completely; recover the existing wall texture beneath its old area.

Concrete typography execution:
Use exactly this sole phrase once, verbatim: 밤에 피는 정원
Set it as one compact, clearly ordered two-line title:
first line is the first two words, kept together with their real word space;
second line is the final word, larger than the first line.
Keep normal top-to-bottom reading, no staggered or reversed word order. Break only at the existing word boundary before the final word.

Place this left-aligned title group in the brighter slate-to-warm wall area at the left of the rising shadow stems, immediately above the real white blossoms and below the left giant shadow flower. The block should fit approximately between the left 6% margin and the rising plant-shadow stem boundary, around the middle-to-lower-left wall: first line near 46% of poster height, larger second line below, completing by about 59% height. The real uppermost white flower begins just below this group; leave a clean gap and do not touch or conceal any real flower or leaf. Use the natural narrowing of the light wedge and nearby rising shadow branches to determine the title's available width and optical alignment. Do not simply relocate the same single centered caption.

Use clean, moderately bold Korean sans-serif with intact Hangul structures and open counters, unambiguous word spacing and proportional line spacing. The first line is roughly half to two-thirds the letter height of the larger final word. This grouping should relate the small real flowering growth below to the garden-sized shadow above. Make every word comfortably readable at a 720px-wide screen view.
Render the letters in matte, deep desaturated charcoal-blue wall paint, visibly contrasting against this lighter illuminated plaster. Their edges remain precise; only subtle real plaster surface relief runs through the pigment. The existing warm-to-cool wall illumination should affect the painted letters naturally, without artificial bevel, glow, drop shadow, embossing, projection blur, fake erosion or torn strokes. The lettering is a surface on the same wall, not bright floating white type. Keep the darker wall shadow from swallowing any letters.

Preserve all photographic elements as closely as possible: the exact three real white flowers and their warm yellow stamens, stem/leaf branching and rooting, real petal forms, their scale and positions, the wall-ground contact, ground strip, crop and blue-gray nighttime photo texture. Keep the existing single low source of warm light from the lower left and its natural wall illumination. Preserve the three large dark projected flower silhouettes, their upward-right enlargement and stem continuity. Their interiors must stay dark: NEVER restore pale or warm stamen-like marks, lit petal colors, or illuminated details within the cast flowers.
Do not add text, captions, labels, numbers, symbols, marks, logos, watermarks, new flowers, props, moon, stars, lamp, halos, artificial lighting effects, border, panel or mockup. The only change is this new title organization and the required restoration of wall surface at its old position.

residuals: Exact individual petal/leaf-to-shadow projection remains uncertain.
Wall grain is coarser and left illumination somewhat warmer/brighter; real plant and ground fine details rerendered.
